ideas.title: A snowball that grows as it rolls
ideas.critique: A snow depth field laid by real snowfall plus a ball that conserves mass as it eats it is a material the island has never had, and the bare grass trail makes it readable in one glance. The risk is that 'rolling body' turns into a sphere sliding on a heightfield with a radius counter, and the stacking turns into a snap-to-place.

ideas.title: Sandcastle against the tide
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Wet versus dry grains holding a wall at different angles is real physics a player can feel, and a slow collapse under the tide is a moment people would watch to the end. DEM with capillary bridges at castle scale is heavy, so expect it to shrink to a blob of particles that never stands up unless the cohesion really works.

ideas.title: Dig a stream to the garden
ideas.critique: Shallow water over a heightfield you can dig is a solid system that more can be built on, and the goal is honest play: water goes where you shaped it and fails where you didn't. Digging toys are a known genre, so it surprises less than it plays, and a top-down film can easily look like a blue line on brown.

ideas.title: Chain reactions on the meadow
ideas.critique: The island already filmed a toppling domino run, so the payoff (a chain falling across the meadow) is a repeat; what is new is that the player builds it from mixed real pieces under IPC contact. Building and failing at piece 31 is a good loop, but on film it will look like the old post again unless the mixed pieces are what you see.

ideas.title: Soap bubbles that show their own thickness
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
same_form: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Thin-film interference driven by a draining thickness is exactly what a path tracer can show and a game engine fakes, and the black cap before the pop is a real, beautiful tell. Light things drifting in the wind are already a post, and the play (float one to a friend) is thin next to the look.

ideas.title: Glassblowing at the workshop
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
same_form: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Hands shaping an object that you then keep and knock repeats the chip-stone recipe; the new part is a viscous shell that stiffens as it cools, which is a hard simulation and likely to become a parametric lathe profile. Glowing glass turning clear under real glass shading could look good.

ideas.title: Carve your own boomerang
same_form: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: This is the voxel carving of the chip stone welded onto the boomerang flight, two of the last ten posts combined, and anyone who knows the island will guess it. Shape-to-aerofoil coupling is a real mechanism, but on film two boomerangs flying differently reads as the old boomerang post twice.

ideas.title: Lightning picks the tallest thing
ideas.critique: A bolt that grows by dielectric breakdown and finds the conductor on its own is new physics and a striking night shot, and the late thunder is a nice touch. The player only gets to plant a rod and wait for a storm, so there is little to do twice, and the scorch and smoulder risk being decals.

ideas.title: The friends play the stones I tuned
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
same_form: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: It is the third post in a row about knocking stones and hearing solved notes; a row of five and a friend with a stick is more of the same mechanism, not a step in what it can do. Tuning to unlock a song gives the toy a real goal, but the film will be stones and notes again.

ideas.title: Lumi gets soaked and shakes dry
ideas.critique: Per-patch feather wetness that changes the material and the gait, with droplets flung off at the speed the spin gives, is a physical character moment the island lacks and serves Lumi's own body. It is a single gag key, and the wetness is likely to end up as one global tint rather than patches that track rain and wading.
